classification.difficultyReason: Find the vertical height difference before applying inverse tangent to an angle of elevation.

content.prompt: A power line is stretched from a pole to the top of a house. The house is 4.1 m high and the power pole is 6.2 m tall. The horizontal distance between the house and the power pole is 12 m. Find the angle of elevation of the top of the power pole from the top of the house to the nearest degree.

spec.description: Pole left and rectangular house right on a common ground level. The power line joins their tops. A dotted horizontal reference extends left from the house-top vertex, with theta between it and the power line. A double-headed arrow below the gap gives 12 m. Decorative source colours are replaced by black; the house width is schematic.
spec.mathematics: Pole height 6.2 m, house height 4.1 m, horizontal separation 12 m; theta is the angle of elevation at the house top.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown theta are visible; no calculated height difference or angle is supplied.

answer.worked:
The vertical height difference is $6.2-4.1=2.1\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{2.1}{12}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2.1}{12}\right)\\\theta&\approx10^{\circ}\quad\text{(nearest degree)}\end{align*}$$
